\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{വാടകയ്ക്കെടുക്കുക} (vāṭakaykkeṭukkuka)}{വാടകയ്ക്കെടുക്കുക (vāṭakaykkeṭukkuka)}]{\ml{വാടകയ്ക്കെടുക്കുക} (vāṭakaykkeṭukkuka) — to hire; to rent}

\label{lesson:ML-C482-vatakaykketukkuka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for a resident, then the Malayalam for a reception desk.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{വാടകയ്ക്കെടുക്കുക}}
\textbf{\ml{വാടകയ്ക്കെടുക്കുക}} — \emph{vāṭakaykkeṭukkuka} — \textquotedblleft{}to hire; to rent\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{ഞങ്ങൾ} \ml{മൂന്ന്} \ml{ദിവസത്തേക്ക്} \ml{ഒരു} \ml{കാർ} \ml{വാടകയ്ക്കെടുത്തു}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ñaṅṅaḷ mūnnŭ divasattēkkŭ oru kār vāṭakaykkeṭuttu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We hired a car for three days.
\end{quote}

Past: \ml{വാടകയ്ക്കെടുത്തു}, \emph{vāṭakaykkeṭuttu}.

Literally to take for rent: \ml{വാടകയ്ക്ക്}, for rent, plus \ml{എടുക്കുക}. To let out is \ml{വാടകയ്ക്ക്} \ml{കൊടുക്കുക}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{വാടകയ്ക്കെടുക്കുക}} (\emph{vāṭakaykkeṭukkuka}) is a Malayalam compound built from \ml{വാടക}, rent, from Sanskrit \emph{bhāṭaka}, \textquotedblleft{}hire\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams), and the native verb \ml{എടുക്കുക}, to take (DEDR 851).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vāṭakaykkeṭukkuka}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vāṭakaykkeṭukkuka}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ñaṅṅaḷ mūnnŭ divasattēkkŭ oru kār vāṭakaykkeṭuttu.} — We hired a car for three days.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for a resident, then the Malayalam for a reception desk, then say \emph{vāṭakaykkeṭukkuka} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{നിക്ഷേപം} (nikṣēpaṁ)}{നിക്ഷേപം (nikṣēpaṁ)}]{\ml{നിക്ഷേപം} (nikṣēpaṁ) — a security deposit; a deposit}

\label{lesson:ML-C482-niksepam}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for a reception desk, then the Malayalam for to hire.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{നിക്ഷേപം}}
\textbf{\ml{നിക്ഷേപം}} — \emph{nikṣēpaṁ} — \textquotedblleft{}a security deposit; a deposit\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{മുറിക്ക്} \ml{ആയിരം} \ml{രൂപ} \ml{നിക്ഷേപം} \ml{കൊടുക്കണം}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{muṟikkŭ āyiraṁ rūpa nikṣēpaṁ koṭukkaṇaṁ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
You must pay a thousand rupees as a deposit for the room.
\end{quote}

The noun of \ml{നിക്ഷേപിക്കുക}, to deposit. In a bank it also means a savings deposit.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{നിക്ഷേപം}} (\emph{nikṣēpaṁ}) is borrowed from Sanskrit \emph{nikṣepa}, \textquotedblleft{}putting down\textquotedblright{}, and so a thing placed in trust (Monier-Williams).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nikṣēpaṁ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nikṣēpaṁ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{muṟikkŭ āyiraṁ rūpa nikṣēpaṁ koṭukkaṇaṁ.} — You must pay a thousand rupees as a deposit for the room.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for a reception desk, then the Malayalam for to hire, then say \emph{nikṣēpaṁ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{നിക്ഷേപം} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A security deposit; a deposit\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{ഒഴിയുക} (oḻiyuka)}{ഒഴിയുക (oḻiyuka)}]{\ml{ഒഴിയുക} (oḻiyuka) — to vacate; to become empty}

\label{lesson:ML-C482-oliyuka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for to hire, then the Malayalam for a security deposit.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{ഒഴിയുക}}
\textbf{\ml{ഒഴിയുക}} — \emph{oḻiyuka} — \textquotedblleft{}to vacate; to become empty\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{രാവിലെ} \ml{പത്ത്} \ml{മണിക്ക്} \ml{മുൻപ്} \ml{മുറി} \ml{ഒഴിയണം}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{rāvile pattŭ maṇikkŭ munpŭ muṟi oḻiyaṇaṁ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
You must vacate the room before ten in the morning.
\end{quote}

Past: \ml{ഒഴിഞ്ഞു}, \emph{oḻiññu}.

The place takes no ending: \ml{മുറി} \ml{ഒഴിയുക}. An empty seat is an \ml{ഒഴിഞ്ഞ} \ml{സീറ്റ്}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{ഒഴിയുക}} (\emph{oḻiyuka}) is native Dravidian, \textquotedblleft{}to leave off, to be free of, to be empty\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 1009). \ml{ഒഴിവ്}, a vacancy, comes from the same root.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{oḻiyuka}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{oḻiyuka}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{rāvile pattŭ maṇikkŭ munpŭ muṟi oḻiyaṇaṁ.} — You must vacate the room before ten in the morning.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for to hire, then the Malayalam for a security deposit, then say \emph{oḻiyuka} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{ഒഴിയുക} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To vacate; to become empty\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{തിരിച്ചുനൽകുക} (tiriccunalkuka)}{തിരിച്ചുനൽകുക (tiriccunalkuka)}]{\ml{തിരിച്ചുനൽകുക} (tiriccunalkuka) — to refund; to give back}

\label{lesson:ML-C482-tiriccunalkuka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for a security deposit, then the Malayalam for to vacate.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{തിരിച്ചുനൽകുക}}
\textbf{\ml{തിരിച്ചുനൽകുക}} — \emph{tiriccunalkuka} — \textquotedblleft{}to refund; to give back\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{യാത്ര} \ml{റദ്ദാക്കിയപ്പോൾ} \ml{അവർ} \ml{പണം} \ml{തിരിച്ചുനൽകി}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{yātra ṟaddākkiyappōḷ avar paṇaṁ tiriccunalki.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
When the trip was cancelled, they refunded the money.
\end{quote}

Past: \ml{തിരിച്ചുനൽകി}, \emph{tiriccunalki}.

\ml{തിരിച്ച്}, back, plus \ml{നൽകുക}, to give. A refund is \ml{പണം} \ml{തിരിച്ചുനൽകൽ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{തിരിച്ചുനൽകുക}} (\emph{tiriccunalkuka}) is a native Dravidian compound of \ml{തിരിച്ച്}, turning back (DEDR 3246), and \ml{നൽകുക}, to give (DEDR 3610).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tiriccunalkuka}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tiriccunalkuka}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{yātra ṟaddākkiyappōḷ avar paṇaṁ tiriccunalki.} — When the trip was cancelled, they refunded the money.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for a security deposit, then the Malayalam for to vacate, then say \emph{tiriccunalkuka} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{തിരിച്ചുനൽകുക} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To refund; to give back\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{ഏർപ്പാട്} (ērppāṭŭ)}{ഏർപ്പാട് (ērppāṭŭ)}]{\ml{ഏർപ്പാട്} (ērppāṭŭ) — an arrangement}

\label{lesson:ML-C482-erppatu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for to vacate, then the Malayalam for to refund.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{ഏർപ്പാട്}}
\textbf{\ml{ഏർപ്പാട്}} — \emph{ērppāṭŭ} — \textquotedblleft{}an arrangement\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{ഹോട്ടലിൽ} \ml{ഭക്ഷണത്തിന്റെ} \ml{ഏർപ്പാട്} \ml{ഉണ്ട്}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{hōṭṭalil bhakṣaṇattinṟe ērppāṭŭ uṇṭŭ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The hotel has arrangements for meals.
\end{quote}

To arrange something is \ml{ഏർപ്പാട്} \ml{ചെയ്യുക} or \ml{ഏർപ്പാടാക്കുക}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{ഏർപ്പാട്}} (\emph{ērppāṭŭ}) is native Dravidian, a noun from the root \ml{ഏൽ}, to take on or undertake (DEDR 905).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ērppāṭŭ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ērppāṭŭ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hōṭṭalil bhakṣaṇattinṟe ērppāṭŭ uṇṭŭ.} — The hotel has arrangements for meals.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for to vacate, then the Malayalam for to refund, then say \emph{ērppāṭŭ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{ഏർപ്പാട്} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}An arrangement\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
